title: Confirmatory R1 (false-done gate) on the OSWorld LibreOffice subset, OSWorld's own task configs, controller, evaluator and Claude runner on the Myco Linux fleet, graded by OSWorld's own evaluate path
ruling: Lead rulings 2026-11-27: 13:55Z (#700 comment 7220110528, approved 14:00Z: each benchmark's own task configs, action server and evaluators, unmodified; Claude via the benchmark's standard computer-use runner; Myco adds only the completion gate before DONE); 14:05Z (#741 comment 7220313158: RETARGET to the Myco Linux fleet with a DesktopEnv provider adapter used by every arm, parity against OSWorld's reference before any live run, measurements; supersedes the environment part of 13:55Z); 14:37Z (#741 comment 7220987945: the accessibility tree and pyautogui/python-xlib in the fleet image and provider; re-measure, also actively driven; keep the parity harness, do not run it); 15:21Z (#741 comment 7221935698: UTM approved as the parity reference hypervisor, a stated deviation; never a Broadcom/VMware account); 15:26Z (#741 comment 7222035806: N3, the self-check arm is the stronger honest baseline, a shell-based re-verification of the end state through the same controller on DONE, a found problem turns DONE into a continue on the same budget; the prompt-suffix variant only as a free secondary ablation); 18:11Z (#741, relayed in the round-3 builder brief: B1, the primary self-check arm dumps the real saved content with one fixed shell command through the same OSWorld controller on DONE, the WAIT turn hands the dump back with a fixed, oracle-free re-verify message, and the model judges on the same turn, token and time budget; nothing saved is not a refusal; the fixed-probe rules and the prompt-suffix variant only as labelled ablations; B2, the hook gets a narrow controller handle with no path to the environment, the evaluator, the task configuration or the cache directory).

rulings.summary: Harness: the benchmark's own task configs, controller, evaluators and standard Claude runner; Myco adds only the DONE gate (approved 14:00Z).
Retarget: OSWorld LibreOffice subset on the Myco Linux fleet; a provider adapter used by every arm; parity before any live run; WAA phase 2; no paid box or second VM.
Scope: a11y tree (GTK3 VCL plugin, AT-SPI bus before Calc) and pyautogui/python-xlib in the image and provider with tests; extended measure.sh incl. actively driven; parity harness kept but not run.

UTM (QEMU/HVF) approved for the parity reference run, recorded as a stated deviation from OSWorld's VMware reference; guest image, controller and evaluator unchanged; nothing downloads until the ~40 GB disk question is answered.

N3 (settles self-check-form): the primary self-check arm is the stronger honest baseline. On DONE it runs its own shell-based re-verification of the end state through the same OSWorld controller and action layer, with no gate, oracle or Myco verdict; a found problem turns DONE into a continue (WAIT plus a fixed, oracle-free message) on the same turn, token and time budget. Pre-registered with what it may and may not read; never the oracle, gold, evaluator output or ground truth. The prompt-suffix variant only as a secondary ablation that costs nothing extra.

rulings.ref: https://github.com/kodingcills/Myco/pull/741 (lead ruling relayed in the round-3 builder brief; not posted as a separate comment)
rulings.summary: B1: the primary self-check arm. On DONE a fixed shell command run through the same OSWorld controller (run_bash_script) dumps the real saved content (cells or text of the files changed during the episode, or 'not saved'); the WAIT turn hands the dump back with a fixed, oracle-free 're-verify your work against the task using this dump' message; the model judges on the same turn, token and time budget as the gate arm, probe calls counted against it (retries stated). Where OSWorld's postconfig saves, nothing saved is not a refusal; ef9d12bd and the config-graded tasks must be able to pass a correct DONE. The fixed-probe rules and the prompt-suffix variant only as labelled ablations, extra trials stated. Never the oracle, fixtures, gold, evaluator code or output, result.txt or any ground truth. B2: no closure over env in the runner patch; a narrow controller handle; tripwires on the environment; a guest-side check that does not rely on the probe hash; W2c2 and W2b2 as regression tests.

harness.name: OSWorld
harness.controller: desktop_env/controllers/python.py#PythonController, talking to OSWorld's own desktop_env/server at the pin, run unmodified inside each fleet desktop

provider.name: myco-fleet
provider.imageDigest: PENDING: the sha256 digest of the fleet image as built by the coordinator; every arm runs this one digest
provider.registration: src/benchmark/upstream/fleet/desktop_env_providers.patch adds the name myco-fleet to desktop_env/providers/__init__.py and to DesktopEnv's clean-start provider set, nothing else; desktop_env.evaluate is untouched
provider.reset: A fresh container per task (no snapshots), as OSWorld's own docker provider resets

harness.pinnedFiles: SHA-256 of every harness file in src/benchmark/upstream/pins.ts OSWORLD_HARNESS.files (patched files: OSWORLD_HARNESS.patchedFiles) and every fleet file in MYCO_FLEET.files; a run on any other bytes, another provider or an unpinned image is ungradable

agentRunner.modifications: None except the DONE gate hook (src/gate-hooks/osworld/myco_done_gate.py), wired by the documented patch surface in docs/benchmark/upstream/gate-hook.md. Arms no-gate and self-check run the same wrapper with the gate bypassed by configuration. The patch passes every arm the same narrow handle, ControllerHandle(env.provider.get_ip_address, env.path_to_vm, PythonController), built without closing over env; arm self-check alone keeps it and uses only its run_bash_script for the pre-registered dump (lead ruling 18:11Z).

model: PENDING: the exact Claude model id passed as --model; it must be one the pinned runner accepts (mm_agents/anthropic/utils.py)

actionLayer.path: AnthropicAgent.predict -> lib_run_single.run_single_example -> DesktopEnv.step -> PythonController.execute_python_command / execute_action; observations from DesktopEnv._get_obs
actionLayer.assertion: Identical across arms: the same runner, environment, provider (myco-fleet, one image digest), controller, action space, observation type and budget in all three arms. The hook takes the agent, never the environment, and returns the agent's actions unchanged except a refused DONE, which becomes upstream's own WAIT special action (a no-op in the guest), in the gate arm on a non-accepting gate verdict and in the self-check arm on the episode's first DONE (its re-verify turn). Only the self-check arm gets a controller handle (ControllerHandle: run_bash_script only, built from the provider's address getter, the image reference and upstream's PythonController class, so it reaches the same desktop_env/server as env.controller), and it calls run_bash_script once per episode for its read-only dump, never an action. Tested with fakes in test/benchmark/osworld-gate-hook.test.ts.

gateInterception.where: Between AnthropicAgent.predict and DesktopEnv.step, in lib_run_single.run_single_example's loop: DoneGate.predict wraps the agent and inspects its returned actions for upstream's DONE special action (AnthropicAgent emits DONE when Claude ends a turn without a tool call).
gateInterception.how: On DONE, the hook calls myco_gate_check with taskId, runId and claim only. verified with accepted:true passes DONE through unchanged (the runner ends the episode and calls env.evaluate()). Anything else (refuted, uncertain, malformed, unreachable) replaces DONE with WAIT and gives the agent one user message with the verdict and reason codes only; the agent continues within the same step budget.
gateInterception.agentFacingReply: verdict and reason codes only; never the gate's prose or corrections

arms.description: (a) OSWorld's standard Claude runner, no gate: DONE is accepted as upstream accepts it.
(b) The same runner; DONE is intercepted and accepted only on a verified gate verdict.

(c) The primary self-check arm, the stronger honest baseline (lead rulings 15:26Z and 18:11Z): the same runner, prompt and budget, no gate, no oracle and no Myco verdict. On the episode's first DONE one fixed shell command, run through the same OSWorld controller, dumps the real saved content; that DONE becomes upstream's WAIT and the next turn hands the dump back with a fixed, oracle-free re-verify message. The model judges: its next DONE goes through. This mirrors the gate arm's structural second chance with the model's own judgement in place of the oracle's.

selfCheck.transport: desktop_env/controllers/python.py#PythonController.run_bash_script (the /run_bash_script endpoint of OSWorld's own desktop_env/server in the fleet desktop, run as the guest user), reached only through src/gate-hooks/osworld/myco_done_gate.py#ControllerHandle. The runner patch builds the handle from the provider's address getter (env.provider.get_ip_address), the image reference (env.path_to_vm) and upstream's PythonController class; each call builds that controller from the address the provider reports, as DesktopEnv._start_emulator builds env.controller, so it reaches the same server every arm's actions go through. The handle exposes run_bash_script only; nothing in it closes over env.
selfCheck.when: On the episode's first DONE, exactly where the gate arm calls the gate. Later DONEs are not checked.
selfCheck.inputs: One only: the whole seconds since the episode started (measured by the hook from the agent's reset, so no guest clock is trusted).
selfCheck.dumpContent: The document files (xlsx, xls, csv, ods, docx, doc, odt, rtf, txt, pptx, ppt, odp, pdf) under the guest user's home directory modified during the episode (at most 4 levels deep; never a hidden directory, a hidden file, a link or another mount; at most 20 files), each with its path, size and save time, then its content: spreadsheet cells by reference with their formulas, document paragraphs, slide text, the leading text of csv, txt and rtf; binary formats (xls, doc, ppt, pdf) are named, not dumped. At most 2,000 characters per file and 6,000 in all. When no document changed: 'NOT SAVED: no document file under the home directory was saved during this episode.'
selfCheck.message: Self-check: before your DONE is accepted, re-verify your work against the task using this dump of the saved state. It lists the document files under your home directory that were saved during this episode, with their cell values or text, or says that none were saved. Check every requirement of the task against it and against the screen. If anything is wrong or missing, fix it. When you are satisfied the task is complete, finish again. This re-check happens once per task.
selfCheck.onDone: The first DONE becomes upstream's own WAIT special action (a no-op in the guest); the next turn starts with one user message: the fixed message, then the dump between <dump> markers (or '(the dump is unavailable: DUMP_UNAVAILABLE)'). Actions after that DONE in the same batch are dropped. The model judges: its next DONE goes through unchanged. The hook decides nothing from the dump's content.
selfCheck.nothingSaved: Never a refusal. On 107 of the 117 tasks OSWorld's own postconfig saves the open document after the episode, and ef9d12bd and the tasks graded from ~/.config/libreoffice have no document at all: a correct DONE passes after the one re-verify turn (test/benchmark/osworld-gate-hook.test.ts, the config-graded case, in the local and the real upstream loop).
selfCheck.failClosed: If the controller raises or returns nothing, the command exits non-zero, or its output lacks the final END record, the re-verify turn still happens with the dump marked unavailable (DUMP_UNAVAILABLE): a first DONE never passes unchecked.
selfCheck.budgetParity: The same --max_steps, token, thinking, trajectory and wall-clock budget as the other arms. Steps: the re-verify turn is the turn of the first DONE, which becomes WAIT and uses that step, as a refused DONE uses its step in the gate arm; the model's next turn is an ordinary turn out of the same --max_steps. The self-check takes it once per episode; the gate arm takes one on each refusal. Model tokens: the dump makes no model call; the message and the dump (at most 6,000 characters) enter the next turn's input, as the gate's codes-only feedback does, under the same --max_tokens and --max_trajectory_length. Probe calls: exactly one run_bash_script call per episode, on the first DONE, none on later DONEs or other turns (tested). Time: the call runs inside the turn of the DONE and counts against the shared wall-clock cap. Its script timeout is 20 s and upstream's controller adds a fixed 100 s HTTP margin, so one attempt is allowed 120 s, the gate client's subprocess timeout for its one call per checked DONE. Upstream's run_bash_script retries a non-200 reply or a connection error (retry_times 3, retry_interval 5 s, a pause after every failed attempt): an unreachable desktop can hold the call for at most 375 s (3 x (120 + 5)) before it fails closed to DUMP_UNAVAILABLE; a read timeout returns at once without a retry. That extra time can fall only on the self-check arm, and only when the desktop is unreachable.
mayRead: the guest user's home directory in the fleet desktop under test, through the handle's run_bash_script, excluding hidden directories, hidden files, links and other mounts: file names, sizes, modification times and the content of document files modified during the episode
mayNotRead: the gate or any Myco oracle or verdict
OSWorld's task configuration (the example JSON: its evaluator, expected values, setup or postconfig)
gold files and expected assets (cloud_file, the DesktopEnv cache directory)
fixtures and any other ground truth
upstream evaluator code (desktop_env evaluators, metrics, getters, DesktopEnv.evaluate) or its output (result.txt, scores)
the environment object (DesktopEnv) or anything reached through it, the provider beyond its address getter, the setup controller, or any controller method other than run_bash_script
selfCheck.enforcedBy: test/benchmark/independence.test.ts (static: the hook imports only json, re, shlex, subprocess and time; its code names no environment, evaluator, task configuration, gold, oracle or score file and no introspection route (__closure__, cell_contents, __globals__, __self__, __dict__, gc, sys, inspect, ctypes); it calls only run_bash_script on its handle; the guest command names no ground truth and starts from $HOME) and test/benchmark/osworld-gate-hook.test.ts (runtime: the handle the patch builds, by evaluating the patch's own expression, reaches no environment, task configuration or cache directory and exposes only run_bash_script; a host audit hook; attribute tripwires on the environment, the provider and the controller; an inotify tripwire on every ground-truth directory and the homes' parent while the guest command runs, independent of its text or hash; the verifier's W2c2, W2b2 and W3 as regression cases)

ablations.label: ABLATION, never the headline baseline (lead ruling 18:11Z)
ablations.description: The round-2 fixed probe: on every DONE one fixed bash script through the same ControllerHandle refuses the DONE (WAIT plus a fixed codes-only message) on a rule below; the hook, not the model, decides.
ablations.implemented: arm self-check-rules in src/gate-hooks/osworld/myco_done_gate.py (SELF_CHECK_PROBE; one run_bash_script call per DONE, the same 120 s allowance)
ablations.inputs: The whole seconds since the episode started, and up to 10 file names with a document extension that the task instruction mentions.
rules: SAVED_FILE_MISSING: a file named in the instruction is not found under the guest user's home directory (at most 4 levels deep, never inside a hidden directory)

SAVED_FILE_FORMAT_MISMATCH: a named file found, or a document saved during the episode, whose bytes do not match its extension (.xlsx/.docx/.pptx must be an Office Open XML container, .ods/.odt/.odp an OpenDocument container, .pdf must start with %PDF-; other document extensions must be readable)
NOTHING_SAVED: no document (xlsx, xls, csv, ods, docx, doc, odt, rtf, txt, pptx, ppt, odp, pdf) under the home directory was modified during the episode
RECHECK_UNAVAILABLE: the controller raised, returned nothing, the probe exited non-zero, or its output lacks the final records (fail closed, as the gate arm fails closed)
ablations.knownBias: NOTHING_SAVED refuses a correct DONE wherever OSWorld's own postconfig saves the document (107 of 117 tasks), and on ef9d12bd and the tasks graded from ~/.config/libreoffice no DONE can pass (tested). This is why it is not the headline baseline.
ablations.cost: 117 extra trials (one per task at n = 117) if run; not run unless separately approved. Its rows are never part of the pre-registered analysis: analyzePublicR1 refuses rows from any arm but the three.

ablations.label: ABLATION, never the headline baseline (lead ruling 18:11Z)
ablations.description: The round-1 prompt-paragraph variant: one paragraph appended through AnthropicAgent's system_prompt_suffix asking the model to verify its saved work before finishing; no structural re-check, no dump.
ablations.implemented: No. Removed in round 2 (last at commit e28aef98); running it needs that arm restored and re-tested first.
ablations.cost: 117 extra trials (one per task at n = 117) if run; not run unless separately approved. Its rows are never part of the pre-registered analysis.

budget: PENDING: one budget for all three arms: --max_steps (the runner default is 15; the Claude example in OSWorld's SETUP_GUIDELINE.md uses 50), --max_tokens, --thinking, --max_trajectory_length, and a wall-clock cap. A refused DONE uses its turn in the gate and self-check arms alike (the self-check's re-verify turn once per episode); the gate call and the self-check dump run inside that turn, cost no step and no model call, and count against the wall-clock cap (arms[2].selfCheck.budgetParity)
subsetRule: Every task id listed in OSWorld's evaluation_examples/test_all.json at the pinned commit under libreoffice_calc, libreoffice_writer and libreoffice_impress, run in OSWorld's own DesktopEnv on the myco-fleet provider. No Myco placement filter; the apps a task needs and the getters its evaluator uses are not exclusions. No task is added or dropped for difficulty, outcome or evaluator type.

grader.description: The upstream evaluation path unmodified: DesktopEnv.evaluate() runs the task's postconfig through its setup controller, its own getters through the in-VM controller and its own metrics, with the FAIL-action rule; lib_run_single writes the score to result.txt. Myco only reads that file (src/benchmark/upstream/r1-grade.ts) and refuses any run whose harness bytes differ from the pin.

parity.rule: Parity must pass before any live run. A pre-declared sample of OSWorld LibreOffice tasks, each with a scripted known-good and known-bad action sequence, is scored by upstream DesktopEnv.evaluate() on the Myco fleet and on the reference environment and recorded per task (src/benchmark/upstream/parity.ts assessParity). Parity passes only when every sample task gives the same status on both; any mismatch is a stated gap, reported with the exact host requirement.

reference.guestImage: Ubuntu-arm.zip from huggingface.co/datasets/xlangai/ubuntu_osworld (the image OSWorld's VMware manager selects on a Mac, desktop_env/providers/vmware/manager.py:27,35 @ 0ad41bee): 12,287,865,453 bytes; 25,215,685,544 bytes unzipped in 27 files (a split vmdk); its Ubuntu.vmx sets memsize 4096, numvcpus 2
reference.deviation: STATED DEVIATION from OSWorld's VMware reference (lead ruling 15:21Z): only the hypervisor differs. The guest image, its in-guest controller and OSWorld's evaluator are unchanged; UTM boots the same split vmdk. Never VMware Fusion or any Broadcom/VMware account.
reference.hostRequirement: docs/benchmark/upstream/host-requirements.md, 'The parity reference run': at least about 40 GB free on the volume holding the VM, 4 GiB guest RAM, one heavy VM at a time under the VM lock, $0 and no accounts

parity.status: Not run. The reference run waits for Tiffany's OK and the ~40 GB disk question (14:37Z, 15:21Z); nothing is downloaded.

gateOracle: PENDING: the gate's oracle family for OSWorld LibreOffice end states (the main build item)
gateOracleConstraint: The gate's oracle must be independent of the upstream evaluator: no import of desktop_env.evaluators (metrics or getters), no shared code, no reading of evaluator output (result.txt, scores) or of gold files (cloud_file expected assets). Enforced for src/gate and src/gate-hooks by test/benchmark/independence.test.ts.
falseDone: The agent says DONE; OSWorld's own evaluate path scores the end state below the pass threshold or the run is ungradable. In the gate arm, the gate either caught it (did not accept) or did not (accepted: a false accept).
primaryOutcome: False accepts in the gate-before-done arm: trials where the gate accepted DONE and OSWorld's evaluate path did not pass. Bar: 0, with the Wilson 95% upper bound on the false-accept rate reported. An accepted claim the evaluator cannot grade counts against the bar.
secondaryOutcomes: Each arm's false-done rate and success rate under the same upstream grader
Paired gate-before-done vs no-gate and gate-before-done vs self-check tables with exact sign tests on discordant pairs (underpowered below 6 discordant pairs, as R2)
Cost per verified task per arm (R7 rule: totals over all trials over the verified count)
evidenceRules: Only LIVE rows graded by OSWorld's evaluate path at the pin count. MOCK, scripted or simulated rows, and rows from the MOCK metric runner (upstream-metric-mock/1), are refused.
Every result line states task set, n, model, baseline, grader, and live or mock.
A frozen pre-registration is never edited after its data exists.
phase2: WAA office subset (64 tasks @ eb220c4dcf64) via WAA's own Windows 11 image, in-VM server, evaluators and runner: deferred, not dropped.
leadRulingPending: asset-license: OSWorld's own setup downloads the seed and gold files from the xlangai/ubuntu_osworld_file_cache dataset, whose terms are unclear (README §1); no live run until ruled
model: the exact Claude model id
budget: the shared step, token, thinking and wall-clock budget
n: 117 (every task in the three LibreOffice domains, one trial each) is this draft's proposal, not ratified; whether to add repetitions is open
pass-threshold: an upstream score of exactly 1.0 is a pass (most OSWorld metrics are 0/1; a few return fractions)
gate-oracle: which gate oracle family the gate-before-done arm uses on these end states, independent of the upstream evaluator
parity-reference-run: the parity reference run (OSWorld's Ubuntu-arm.zip in UTM) waits for Tiffany's OK and the ~40 GB disk question (15:21Z); parity must pass before any live run
model-access: the pinned runner calls the Anthropic API (or Bedrock/Vertex) with a key; M2's rule is $0 API on the Claude Ultra plan, so how the runner reaches the model needs a ruling
